bodyA:
Create a production-ready transparent PNG game sprite atlas derived faithfully from the two provided approved FUTAGO reference images. This is the separated LEFT member of the existing fused twin monster, the narrow clean-shaven pale face with straight messy dark hair, ragged dark brown/gray clothing, asymmetrical elongated hooked arms, bony organic rib patterns. Keep that exact individual's facial identity, colors and worn clothing. The story mechanic is that the existing fused pair separates along its central organic seam; do not make a new character and do not duplicate the whole fused pair. Every cell must contain just this ONE identifiable head and its own separated body, with the partner entirely absent. The exposed seam is dry dark scarred tissue and closed bony ribs, no fresh blood or new gore. Grim realistic hand-painted post-apocalyptic style matching reference, crisp silhouette at a runtime height of 150 px.

Deliver one wide atlas with EXACTLY 7 equally sized columns and EXACTLY 2 equally sized rows, preferably 3360x960. No visible grid, words, labels, numbers, borders, floor, scenery, shadow rectangle, white/black matte or checkerboard painting: actual RGBA transparency in all empty space. All complete bodies, fingertips and feet stay inside their own cells with a clear transparent gutter. Same body size and foot baseline in each cell; death remains on the same floor baseline. Camera is fixed side-view with slight three-quarter visibility.

Top row: facing LEFT, the head and primary attack point left. Bottom row: the identical seven poses facing RIGHT. Columns in each row, precisely in order: 1 standing breathing idle; 2 walking step A with left foot forward; 3 walking opposite step B with right foot forward; 4 clearly readable attack preparation, claw pulled BACK behind shoulder; 5 attack impact with the SAME claw reaching straight FORWARD toward the facing direction; 6 recoiling from a hit, still standing; 7 fallen defeated body on the ground. The two walking poses must be clearly different. This atlas must show 14 separate complete one-headed figures, never paired figures or two heads in any cell. Retain anatomical and clothing continuity throughout.
